title: The plan your conversation changes
meaning: A wish to make words dependable helps you speak concretely, although discovering different expectations can come as a powerful surprise.
text: The more closely you discuss a promise, the more clearly you may see how differently each person heard it. The Empress in the physical position of Vishuddha develops the conversation, giving a suggestion examples and living detail. The Emperor in energy supports a conscientious wish to understand what you are responsible for and what you can actually promise. The Tower in emotions describes the shock when a familiar “We agreed” suddenly loses its foundation. Concrete words can clarify a question even when the first experience of clarity feels abrupt.

Suppose you discuss a promise to help rearrange a room. One person imagines a short evening; the other pictures a whole day off sorting belongings. As you name the details, the mismatch becomes visible. **A dependable promise begins with hearing the difference.** You can specify a realistic amount of involvement and agree again with an understanding of what each person had previously meant by the same sentence.

The difficulty is experiencing this discovery as the cancellation of everything said before. You may want to prove immediately that your version was obvious, turning a conversation about practical help into a defence of the past. Conscientious intentions can remain on both sides. Distinguishing an earlier assumption from a new promise can help more than securing a single permissible interpretation of the old phrase.
